acceptance_criteria.criterion: The view renders a two-panel layout with independently scrollable sidebar and main content.
The sidebar lists all workspaces grouped by project (collapsible groups).
Sidebar items for workspaces with notes are visually distinguished from those without.
Clicking a sidebar item for a workspace with notes scrolls the main panel to its card.
Clicking a sidebar item for a workspace without notes creates a new empty card and focuses it.
Each note card displays a clickable workspace ID that links to the workspace detail view.
Each card textarea auto-saves after 1000 ms of inactivity with a status indicator.
Saving a note as empty removes the card and updates the sidebar indicator.
On initial load, only workspaces with non-empty notes show cards in the main panel.

summary: Created gui/public/js/views/notes-collected.js — the two-panel Notes Collected view. Left sidebar lists all workspaces grouped by collapsible project groups (data from api.notes.list() + normaliseNotesResponse()); workspaces with notes carry a .has-notes class. Right main panel shows editable note cards on initial load only for non-empty notes. Clicking a sidebar item with an existing card scrolls to it; clicking one without a card creates a new empty card and focuses it. Each card has a workspace-detail link in the header, a textarea, a 1000 ms debounced auto-save via api.workspaces.update(), and an aria-live status indicator. Saving empty removes the card and clears the sidebar indicator. Empty-state message shown when no cards are present.
Registered the #/notes route in app.js and added the 'Notes' nav link in index.html (before Error Log).

Added .workspace-notes-* CSS to styles.css (the workspace-detail notes textarea section had no styles). Added full .notes-view, .notes-sidebar, .notes-sidebar-*, .notes-main, .notes-card, and .notes-empty-state / .notes-loading / .notes-error CSS.
Created gui/public/js/views/notes-collected.test.mjs with 19 tests covering all 9 acceptance criteria (AC1–AC9). All 19 pass.
Full test suite: 780 backend + 172 GUI tests pass (19 new), 0 failures. tsc --noEmit clean.

comments.note: gui/public/js/views/notes-collected.js: the `sidebar` variable is forward-declared as `let` so that the `handleSave` and `handleCardEmpty` closures (defined before it is assigned) can reference it safely. This is a well-understood JS closure pattern but worth noting for future readers — the assignment always completes before any user-triggered callback can fire.

gui/public/css/styles.css: the .workspace-notes-* CSS classes (workspace-notes-section, workspace-notes-textarea, workspace-notes-label, workspace-notes-status) were referenced by workspace-detail.js but had no corresponding CSS rules before this WP. Added them as part of this implementation since the styles.css section was clearly the right place. This was existing debt from WP-007.

notes-collected.js uses `color-mix(in srgb, ...)` for the textarea focus background in styles.css. This is supported in all modern browsers (Chrome 111+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.2+) but falls back gracefully — the textarea simply keeps its default surface colour. A future improvement could provide an explicit fallback for older browsers.

comments.note: AC4 test only verifies no duplicate card is created on a second sidebar click; it does not assert that scrollIntoView() is called. The implementation does invoke scrollIntoView, which is stubbed in the test environment. Acceptable given jsdom limitations.

notes-collected.js: 'Save failed.' status text is never auto-hidden — it persists until the user types again. Not a failing AC (the spec only requires a status indicator), but a minor UX inconsistency compared to 'Saved' which auto-hides after 3 seconds.
No test explicitly exercises the api.notes.list() error path (.notes-error element). The implementation handles it correctly; the gap is in test coverage only.
No observations — code is clean and consistent. All dynamic text uses textContent (XSS-safe), URLs use encodeURIComponent, and the forward-declared sidebar closure pattern is sound.
